messages:
dana: Heads-up — saw steady KV cache growth on a 50k-token chat replay test. Memory climbs even after the session ends, looks like small non-reclaimed blocks piling up. :thinking:
cheng: Ugh. Is this the same cluster where we flipped the batching heuristic last week? We changed batch coalescing, might be producing many small allocations for KV slices.
maya: I profiled one of the hosts -> attached a snippet from heap profiler: `gc_bins: {size_64: 412, size_128: 230, size_256: 1210, size_512: 5400, >512: 89}`. Notice the spike in 256/512 buckets after long-context runs.
ben: Interesting. Could be fragmentation due to varying KV entry lifespans. Long-context sessions pin large KV pages while short queries churn tiny ones -> allocator splits pages and leaves holes.
dana: Agreed. I ran an experiment with lifespan tagging in the allocator: mark entries with estimated lifespan (short/long) and prefer packing same-lifespan into same blocks. Results: peak RSS -12% and tail latency unchanged. Quick logs: `reclaim_cycles: 120ms -> 35ms`, `coalesce_ops: 18 -> 72` (more coalescing is good here).
cheng: Nice. Can you paste the config you used? Want to try toggling thresholds.
dana: Sure — config I tested (very rough):
```
kv_reclaim:
  lifespan_buckets: [short, medium, long]
  short_threshold_ms: 5000
  medium_threshold_ms: 60000
  coalesce_window_ms: 200
  aggressive_backfill: true
```
maya: Two quick notes: 1) long sessions have pinned KV for inference prefixes (reused across steps) so marking them 'long' makes sense. 2) aggressive_backfill increases CPU usage from coalescing — saw +7% p50 CPU in that host.
ben: There's also the point about block sizing. We currently use fixed 4KB sub-blocks inside 2MB superblocks. If we adapt sub-block granularity by workload (grow sub-block to 8KB for long-lifespan hot regions) we may reduce fragmentation. But need to simulate.
perf-bot: perf/regression check queued -> benchmark suite: kv-lifespan-reclaim-v2 (100k chats). ETA ~18m.
mem-bot: Alert (2145123650): host-42 RSS > 85% of baseline after test run; reclaim pass not triggered for 12m.
dana: Observed pattern: after heavy mixing of short and long contexts, allocator ends with a lot of 256/512 bins that are 60-90% full and scattered. Compaction isn't triggered because reclaim policy is time-based, not fragmentation-based.
cheng: Proposal time: add fragmentation-driven compaction trigger + lifespan-aware placement. Two heuristics: (A) if free_frag_ratio > 0.25 within a superblock, async coalesce adjacent free slots; (B) prefer packing by lifespan bucket at allocation time.
maya: I also want a hard cap TTL for 'short' entries so they auto-expire earlier (helps reuse). Maybe 2s for short.
ben: We should be careful with eviction order: prefer evicting short entries first, but don't evict those that are part of an in-flight KV chain for streaming decode. Need a pinned bit and an age counter.
dana: I ran a micro-sim of (A) and (B) across 10k simulated sessions: fragmentation metric (frag_index) dropped 38%, steady-state RSS down 9%. But compaction increased transient CPU by ~10%.
cheng: Tradeoff seems acceptable for Dedicated customers where memory predictability matters. For hosted low-tier, maybe run conservative variant (only pack long-lifespan).
maya: Another edge: kernel selection changes that allow larger per-request KV allocation (we changed to vectorized KV copy recently) made some allocations bypass the allocator and come from a slab cache — that might circumvent reclamation. Need to patch to annotate those allocations with lifespan too.
dana: Good catch. I'll audit kernel paths and ensure annotations travel with allocations.
ben: Next steps: 1) dana to open RFC with the two heuristics + config knobs and perf logs; 2) cheng/maya to test on canary with perf-bot checks; 3) add unit tests for pinned bit and lifespan bucket packing.
dana: Will open RFC today and include SIM results + heap profiles. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
